sections.overview: Panolis flammea is a noctuid moth whose caterpillars eat pine needles; native in Europe, it can become a forest pest during outbreaks.
sections.identification: The regional moth account calls the adult unmistakable but supplies no diagnostic features; use a specialist guide for visual identification.
sections.habitat: It lives in pine forests and plantations; outbreaks have been documented on Scots pine and introduced lodgepole pine in Scotland.
sections.diet: Larvae eat pine needles, especially Scots and lodgepole pine; one Scottish account also lists larch as an occasional host.
sections.behavior: Outbreaks can cause extensive defoliation in susceptible plantations; host tree and site conditions influence the risk.
sections.reproduction: In Dumfries and Galloway it has one generation yearly, overwinters as a pupa and has larvae from May to July; timing may differ elsewhere.
sections.ecology: It overlaps ecologically with the Pine Looper, Bupalus piniaria, already profiled here: both feed on pine needles, but they are different moths with different life cycles.
sections.conservation: Its forestry importance is episodic, not a measure of global conservation status; historical outbreaks have been concentrated in particular regions and host stands.
